rows.why: S1 depends on how loosely stored values are cleaned before matching. Item 2 trims and lowercases, so "Draft", " PUBLISHED ", "Merged" and "claimed" read as their statuses.

S2 settles which old spellings count as aliases. Item 3's pick accepts only 'in review'. So "under_review" (cleaned to 'under review') and "LIVE" ('live') would read as null, not review and published.

Item 1 asks what an unrecognised stored value reads as. Its pick returns null for anything that is not a status or known alias, with no nearest-match guessing. So 'closed', 'drafts', 'revew' and blank values read as no status. Item 9 covers only the empty case.
S4 is the plain case where an exact status is stored unchanged. No item asks this. Item 4 is about values that are not exactly a status, and any answer to it still stores 'review' as 'review'.

Item 4 asks whether writing accepts other casing, padding or old spellings. Its pick throws on anything but an exact lowercase enum value, so 'Review', 'in-review', ' draft' and 'closed' are refused. Item 5 adds that the error message contains the value.

Item 7 asks how unreadable values are listed in a bulk read: raw or cleaned, deduplication, and order. Its pick lists raw stored strings, deduplicated exactly and sorted, which matches 'each distinct original value once, sorted, exactly as it was stored'. Item 6 covers only the row-with-null part.
